segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We mentioned that with future context, we can talk about the future using the present.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: For example, we had tomorrow, which was...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Mañana. Good. We had later or more late, which was...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Más tarde. We had tonight or this night...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Esta noche. Good. Another one is pronto. Pronto. What do you think pronto means?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Soon. Yeah, you hear in English sometimes "Get here pronto!", no? It's get here soon. So pronto is also future context. What was the verb to see or to view?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good. The "I" version is a tiny bit irregular, it's veo. Veo. So you have v-e-o. So it's not vo, as it should be, or bo, it was too short, it became veo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: V-e-o. Veo or veo. How would you say: I'm seeing her later. I'm seeing her later.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: That means: I see she later.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: La veo más tarde. I'm seeing her tonight.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. La veo esta noche. We are seeing her soon. We are seeing her soon.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Oh sorry, it should be ve- vemos?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So no guessing. No guessing at all. It's the only rule, ah?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. La vemos pronto. What if we say: we're seeing, we will see them soon, but with this them, we mean a female group. We're seeing them soon.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Las vemos pronto. He is seeing them soon, and this them, they are still females. He is seeing them soon.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Now make it a question. Are you seeing them soon? The female them.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: ¿Las ves pronto? Aren't you seeing them soon?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: ¿No las ves pronto? Why aren't you seeing them soon?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. ¿Por qué no las ves pronto? Very good. So we saw that with future context, we don't need the future. If we don't have future context, we can still use the present to talk about the future using this "I go" or "I'm going", which is present, but we can use it to talk about the future in Spanish as we do in English. I'm going to see her, we're talking about the future. We're going to see her.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So let's practice that. How would you say: we are going to see her.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Are you going to see him soon? Speaking informally, are you going to see him soon? So you can't work with ir, which is to go, you should probably work with vamos and work backwards.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. ¿Vas a verlo pronto? The word for "us" is nos. Nos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So how would you say: are you going to see us soon? Are you going to see us soon? And we're still speaking informally.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good. ¿Vas a vernos pronto? Where else could that nos go?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good. ¿Nos vas a ver pronto? Aren't you going to see us soon?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. ¿No vas a vernos pronto? or ¿No nos vas a ver pronto? either way. Why aren't you going to see us soon?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: ¿Por qué no vas a vernos pronto?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So we've seen that we can use the present to talk about the future using going to or also using future context, word like tomorrow, next week. Next week is the week that comes, and the week is la semana. La semana.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How would you say the week that comes? So what is the word for "that", which is the same as "what"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Que. La semana que, the week that, the week which, comes, and here we mean the week comes, so it's it comes. So what is "it comes"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So next week is la semana que viene. The week that comes. La semana que viene. So you could say: let's speak. And to say let's speak, we know from vamos, you can just use the "we" form. So to speak is...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Let's speak next week. Let's speak the week that comes.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Hablamos la semana que... and now I've forgotten come.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: It's okay. Okay, if we forgot it, we need to find it again. That's not any problem. Every time we do find it, we strengthen that process, and that's what we need. Not to remember the word, the process we need to strengthen. I want you to know how to find to come, and then to go from there: it comes. Take your time to find "it comes".

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Viene. Let's speak the coming week.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: At the moment you have you have the whole sentence in your mind and you want to translate it. Now this process works when you're memorizing. But we're not memorizing. We're doing something else. We're building. So we must reduce it down to the smallest piece we could possibly think about, think about that piece, get it out, then forget it. So the first bit is: we speak, let's speak.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Viene. Good. Hablamos la semana que viene. What was to see or to view?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Vemos. If you want to say we see each other, you say we see us. Nos can mean us, ourselves, each other, can mean all of that. Nos. So how do you say we see ourselves?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Nos vemos. This is a way of saying goodbye in Spanish: ¡Nos vemos! We see each other. Now the future context here is the fact that you're saying goodbye. But we're using present, because we know when we say nos vemos, we don't mean we're seeing each other right now, we mean we will see each other again. We're not even mentioning that future context, but it's working, it's allowing us to use the present there. ¡Nos vemos! ¡Chao! Or you might want to say: we will see each other next week. How would you say that? So piece by piece. We see each other - I want all of your mental energy on that and not thinking yet about next week, how you will say that. What you're worried about right now at this moment is how you're going to say: we see ourselves, and even before that, just we see.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: So it's vemos, and it's nos vemos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. The week that comes. So the week...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. ¡Nos vemos la semana que viene! So you see it's not important to remember viene. We don't want to remember viene. This is useless. In fact, if we memorize viene, we're just going to be glazing over the problem, ah? What we want to internalize is the process of, "Oh, how do I find this?"

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So we've seen that we can use the present to talk about the future using either ir a - to go to, voy a, vamos a, va a - or using some future context.
